FortiADC workspace

The FortiADC ADOM mirrors the appliance's own left menu so you can browse, create, edit and delete FortiADC objects live on a selected device, with a dry-run preview before every form-based write.

What is it?#

The FortiADC workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiADC application delivery controllers. Its sidebar reproduces the FortiADC GUI's own left menu (Server Load Balance, Link Load Balance, Global Load Balance, Web Application Firewall, and so on), so anyone who knows the appliance knows where to look. Every list is read live from the FortiADC you have selected: there is no local cache for FortiADC objects.

What does it do?#

  • Dashboard (/adc/) — a device picker with every FortiADC you may see, plus an overview card per menu section with a link to each entry. The subtitle counts the object types and sections that are available.
  • Menu pages (/workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>) — one page per entry of the FortiADC's measured menu, drawn in FortiADC's layout: its tabs, its Create New menu and its columns (for example, on 7.6.7, Server Load Balance > Real Server Pool has the tabs Real Server Pool, Real Server and Server SSL). Each tab lists the objects live from the device.
  • Dialogs — each object opens in FortiADC's own dialog, with its child tables (such as pool members) edited in place. The classic pages use the FortiADC object editor.
  • Wizard — on Server Load Balance → Virtual Server, builds real servers, a pool, the pool members and the virtual server in one step. See Guided virtual server wizard.
  • Signatures — a read-only overview of the FortiADC Web Attack Signature policies, at the end of the FortiADC menu group.
  • Naming — the FortiADC naming patterns (reference only), opened from the Administrator group.
  • API — the FortiADC endpoint catalog and live API console. See Product API pages.
  • Not in GUI, but in CLI — an entry at the end of the device's menu (only Signatures follows it) opens the per-device page: every object the FortiADC serves over REST that no page of its own GUI reads on its build, each with its rows, read from the device when the page opens (read only, secrets never shown). See Not in GUI, but in CLI.
  • VS Inspector — on the appliance page, a tree per virtual server that follows every reference to its end. See VS Inspector.

The menu in the sidebar#

The FortiADC group is the selected appliance's own menu, drawn from the GUI layout measured on its firmware build (the layouts arrive with the knowledge packs):

  • All pages — a grid with every page of the menu, one card per top-level group.
  • The FortiADC menu tree in the device's own order (Server Load Balance, Link Load Balance, Global Load Balance, Web Application Firewall, Network Security, Network, System and so on), one entry per page the build has.
  • Not in GUI, but in CLI — see Not in GUI, but in CLI.
  • Signatures — SATOM's live overview of the Web Attack Signature policies, for holders of protection.view.

With no FortiADC selected, or none with a layout for its build, the group holds Signatures only. Administrators can hide monitor and device-managed pages from the menu under Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus (see ADOM Menus).

The classic menu pages#

The /adc/m/<item> pages follow a fixed tree modelled on the FortiADC 8.0 GUI. Since 3.1 the sidebar no longer draws it: an old address opens the measured page that shows the same objects, where the selected appliance has one, and ?classic=1 opens the classic page. A classic entry only exists when the FortiADC endpoint registry contains at least one of its object types.

Requirements#

  • At least one appliance registered with kind fortiadc under Appliances. Without one, the dashboard shows No FortiADC appliances registered yet and menu pages cannot list objects.
  • A selected FortiADC. If the ADOM holds exactly one FortiADC you can see, it is used automatically. With two or more, pick one on the dashboard or from the Device entry in the sidebar.
  • The appliance credentials must let SATOM log in to the FortiADC REST API.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the dashboard and menu pages, read object lists and object details The legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example network.view)
Create New, Wizard, Save → Apply to <device>, Clone, Delete, row edits; on the classic pages New (guided), Review & save and Save raw JSON to device Any granular key that grants configuration writes, for example network.edit or network.apply (these map to the legacy config_write key)
Signatures page protection.view
Naming page users.manage
API → Registry & console (sidebar entry and page) registry.view; see Product API pages

Users without write permission still see the lists and open each object, but the Wizard, Clone, Delete and ⟳ buttons are not rendered and Edit reads View; on the classic pages the raw JSON box is read-only. Calling a write endpoint directly returns HTTP 403. A user with no read permission gets HTTP 403 on every FortiADC page. Users without users.manage do not see the Administrator group, and users without protection.view do not see Signatures (opening /adc/signatures directly returns HTTP 403).

The built-in Viewer (readonly) profile can browse, open Signatures and the API console. The Operator profile can also create, edit and delete objects. Only Administrator sees the Administrator group with Naming.

How to use#

Select a FortiADC#

  1. Open the product selector and choose FortiADC, or click FortiADC under ADOMs in the Global sidebar.
  2. On the dashboard, find the device under FortiADC devices and click Select. The card shows the badge selected and the button changes to Selected.
  3. To change device later, click the Device entry at the top of the sidebar.

Browse a menu entry#

  1. In the sidebar, open the FortiADC group, then a group of the device's menu (for example Server Load Balance), and click a page (for example Real Server Pool). FortiADC → All pages shows the whole menu as a grid, one card per top-level group.
  2. The breadcrumb shows the FortiADC menu path (FortiADC / Server Load Balance / Real Server Pool) and the header the device and its firmware. The tabs across the top are FortiADC's own (on 7.6.7: Real Server Pool, Real Server and Server SSL). Click a tab to load it.
  3. The rows are read live from the device: the toolbar shows a live badge and the object count. Type in Search to filter the visible rows.
  4. Click ⟳ to read the device again (Re-read from <device>.).
  5. Click a row to select it; double-click it, press Enter or click Edit to open it in FortiADC's dialog.

The columns are the ones FortiADC's GUI shows on that page, in its order. A FortiView page draws live monitor data, not configuration: it says so and links to the same page on the device.

Create an object#

  1. Open the page and the tab for the object type.
  2. Click Create New (where FortiADC's menu offers several kinds, pick one). FortiADC's dialog opens.
  3. Fill in the name and the fields, click Save, check Review the change, then click Apply to <device>. SATOM re-reads the object and shows the verdict: Verified on the device, Not applied (naming the value the device kept) or Not verified.

For a virtual server, the Wizard button on Server Load Balance → Virtual Server is usually quicker. See Guided virtual server wizard.

Delete an object from a list#

  1. Select the row and click Delete.
  2. Confirm Delete "<name>"?. SATOM sends a dry run and shows the request; nothing has been removed yet.
  3. Confirm Apply this delete to the device now?. SATOM deletes the object, re-reads the device, and the toast reports the verdict before the list reloads.

Review the Web Attack Signature policies#

  1. Open FortiADC → Signatures (the last entry of the group).
  2. The table lists each signature policy with Status, Categories, Sub-categories, Disabled sigs, High action, Medium action, Low action and Exception. Predefined policies carry a built-in badge.
  3. Click a name or the pencil button to open the policy in the object editor. Create New opens a blank Web Attack Signature policy.

The device's own list of these policies is the measured page Web Application Firewall → Known Web Attacks (tab Web Attack Signature on 7.6.7).

Inspect a virtual server (VS Inspector)#

  1. Open the FortiADC in Appliances and click VS Inspector under Appliance Actions.
  2. Choose the source: - Live (REST) reads the device. It starts from the virtual servers and follows their references outward: each table is read once, child tables are read only for the groups a virtual server actually reaches, and the whole walk uses one reused connection. - From last rediscovery draws the same tree from the last sweep and its depth capture, without contacting the device. The header shows the sweep and the depth capture it used.
  3. Each virtual server is drawn to the end of every reference: content routing (with its match conditions) → pool → members → real server and health checks; client SSL profile → certificate group → certificates → intermediate CA; auth policy → user group → RADIUS / LDAP / local user; WAF sub-profiles, method, persistence, profiles, SNAT and schedule pools. A reference to an object the device does not have is shown as not found on the device.

Both sources draw identical trees. The live read is the faster one now: on a lab FortiADC with 15 virtual servers it fell from 7.6 s and 90 reads to 0.8 s and 70 reads.

Certificate-group, CA-group and schedule-group members exist only in FortiADC child tables. Without a depth capture, From last rediscovery warns that those groups are drawn without members: run a rediscovery with Capture full depth: every child table (REST) on.

Edit FortiADC naming patterns#

Open Administrator → Naming. The page opens on the FortiADC product and lists the FortiADC naming elements (for example Real Server with the default pattern rs-{name}). See Naming for how patterns work.

The FortiADC patterns are reference only: the page says so in a note (Reference only. FortiADC patterns document your convention; the FortiADC object editor and the virtual-server wizard do not fill in or check names from them.). You type every object name yourself.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Appliance kind Must be fortiadc for the device to appear in this ADOM Yes fortiadc
Host / port Where SATOM reaches the FortiADC REST API Yes 192.0.2.20 / 443
Username / password Credentials used for POST /api/user/login Yes satom-api
v query parameter Opens a tab of a menu page by position (0 is the first tab) No /workspace/<id>/fwgui/slb.pool?v=1

Example#

🧪Example — Check the back-ends of a pool

  1. Select adc-01 on the FortiADC dashboard.
  2. Go to FortiADC → Server Load Balance → Real Server Pool.
  3. The Real Server Pool tab lists pool-web with FortiADC's columns. Double-click pool-web.
  4. FortiADC's dialog opens; its member table lists each pool member.
  5. Switch to the Real Server tab to see the address of each real server.

Result#

  • Reads change nothing and leave no audit entry.
  • Every write that reaches the device is recorded in the Audit Log with the FortiADC appliance and the object, for example adc.create, adc.update, adc.delete, adc.row_create, adc.row_update, adc.row_delete or adc.wizard_create.
  • Lists are not stored: the next visit reads the device again.
  • A rediscovery with Capture full depth files the child-table rows of every parent object (pool members, certificate-group members, content routing and rewriting conditions, schedule-group members…) in SATOM's deep layer, where Analysis and the API library read them. See Discovery and rediscovery.

Troubleshooting#

"No FortiADC selected — object lists are read live from a device."#

Possible causes - No device is selected, and the ADOM holds more than one FortiADC. - No FortiADC is registered, or the one that is registered is in maintenance mode and hidden from you.

Solution 1. Click Pick one on the FortiADC dashboard and select a device. 2. If the dashboard says No FortiADC appliances registered yet, register the appliance with kind fortiadc under Administrator → Appliances (or Operations → Appliances without the administrator capability).

Verification — the FortiADC group of the sidebar shows the device's menu, and its pages show a live badge.

"Device error: HTTP 401" or "Device error: device errcode …"#

Possible causes - Wrong credentials on the appliance record (HTTP 401). - The device refused the read and returned a negative error code. - The object type does not exist on this FortiADC build (HTTP 404).

Solution 1. Check the appliance credentials under Administrator → Appliances (or Operations → Appliances). 2. If one tab fails and the others work, check the endpoint in the FortiADC API catalog and disable or correct it (see Product API pages).

Verification — after ⟳ the tab lists objects instead of the error (on a measured page, <device> did not answer: …; on a classic page, the red banner).

"is not served by fortiadc …"#

Possible causes — the registry records that the object type is not available on the firmware build the device runs.

Solution — check the API versions page of the FortiADC API catalog, or pick a device on a build that serves the type.

Verification — the tab lists objects instead of the error banner.

A menu entry or tab is missing#

Possible causes - No GUI layout for the device's build has been imported: the FortiADC group then holds Signatures only. - The device's build has no such page in its own GUI, or the layout was refused on import. - An administrator hid monitor or device-managed pages under Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus.

Solution 1. Check that the knowledge packs are up to date. 2. Check ADOM Menus. 3. A bookmark to the classic page (/adc/m/<item>?classic=1) still opens it.

Verification — the page appears in the FortiADC group and in All pages.

Signatures returns "403 Forbidden"#

Possible causes — the Signatures page requires protection.view, and your profile does not have it.

Solution — ask an administrator to add protection.view to your profile. The built-in Viewer, Operator and Administrator profiles have it.

Verification — the page lists the signature policies.

Advanced#

Advanced How lists and columns are built
  • The menu is the FortiADC GUI layout measured on the device's firmware build, delivered by the knowledge packs; it is cached for 60 seconds per product and build. The page's tabs, Create New menu and columns are the layout's.
  • Each tab is one live read of its collection on the device; nothing is cached, and ⟳ only drops the few-second read memo.
  • On the classic /adc/m/<item> pages (?classic=1), the menu tree lives in code and is resolved against the FortiADC registry (product = fortiadc), and columns are derived from the first object in the response: the identity (mkey, name or id) plus up to six scalar fields, preferring status, type, interface, ip, address, port, pool, profile, method, mode, comments and comment. A device refusal is shown as a banner, never as an empty list.
Advanced Build evidence (API library)
  • The FortiADC schema adapter is verified against a lab FortiADC on 7.6.7 build0676 (2026-10-13). The schema harvest adds a read-only REST shape probe of the objects the rediscovery sweep does not read: top-level objects, and child tables by ?pkey=. A 404 at a child path is not recorded as absent, because FortiADC serves some children only inside the parent row.
  • FortiADC's REST names some fields differently from its CLI (pool for load-balance-pool). Those renames are measured per build (7.6.7 and 8.0.4) and shown as one field under the REST name; an unmeasured build gets no renames. See API library.
Advanced ADOM scoping
  • Entering any /adc/ or /adc/api/ page switches the browser tab to the FortiADC ADOM.
  • In the FortiADC ADOM, pages outside the FortiADC allow-list redirect to the FortiADC dashboard.
  • Only appliances of kind fortiadc are visible. Opening another product's appliance by id returns 404.
  • The firmware library (Administrator → Firmware) is live in the FortiADC ADOM since 3.1.0: FortiADC appliances offer Upgrade and Boot Partition through the same runbook as FortiWeb. To see virtual servers, use FortiADC → Server Load Balance → Virtual Server.
